Summary: SOS reachable in one tap, no blocking pop-ups on the trip screen (safety escalation)
Description:
Affected Flow: Active Trip screen and Emergency SOS trigger

Hypotheses:
App dialog manager renders non-dismissible modal notifications over the active trip view, overlaying and blocking the touch target of the SOS floating action button.
Notification stack fails to respect emergency view hierarchy z-indexing during ride state transitions.

Proposed Change:
Enforce top-level z-index window for SOS button that bypasses any in-app notification overlays. Implement persistent 1-tap SOS in system notification bar during active rides.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–3: Inspect WindowManager and DialogFragment hierarchy on trip activity. Days 4–8: Refactor SOS to persistent non-blocking overlay. Days 9–14: Test on multiple Android OEM overlays and ship hotfix.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. SOS button is tap-responsive within 500ms under any active modal or notification state.
2. In-app popups cannot obscure the emergency action container.
3. Verified in automated Espresso UI tests.
Metrics to Measure: Zero blocked SOS events; 100% successful trigger within 1 tap under stress testing.

Summary: Fix app not opening or getting stuck after updates; reproduce upgrade path; staged rollout gate
Description:
Affected Flow: App Cold Launch & Post-Upgrade SQLite/SharedPrefs Migration

Hypotheses:
Room/SQLite schema migration failure on upgrade causes unhandled SQLiteConstraintException or IllegalStateException during Application.onCreate().
Cached authentication tokens or Room database corrupted on delta APK upgrade, forcing users to uninstall and reinstall to wipe app data.
Android 14/15/16 background initialization changes causing ANR on modern Pixel/OnePlus devices.

Proposed Change:
Wrap local database upgrade migrations with automated fallback recovery (repair cache rather than crash). Set up CI upgrade tests (v12.14 -> v12.18 -> v12.19). Enforce staged rollout gates (freeze if crash-free sessions drop below 99.5%).

First 14 Days:
Days 1–4: Reproduce upgrade path in QA emulator matrix; analyze Crashlytics launch exceptions. Days 5–9: Fix Room schema migration and corrupted state handler. Days 10–14: Staged rollout (5% -> 20% -> 100%) with automated ANR/crash halt.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. 100% of schema migration test matrices pass in automated CI across 5 prior versions.
2. Crash-free user rate >= 99.5% on canary 5% rollout.
3. Automatic database corruption recovery clears bad cache without crashing.
Metrics to Measure: Crash-free user rate (target: >= 99.5%); reduction in update-related review complaints.

Summary: Fix logout loop and OTP delivery; add resend and a 'your company has not added you' message
Description:
Affected Flow: Authentication, Session Renewal, and Employee Account Onboarding

Hypotheses:
Session refresh token expires prematurely or encounters 401 on background sync, causing silent logout back to welcome screen.
SMS gateway carrier routing failures or DND throttling drop OTP delivery without client fallback.
Unregistered enterprise employees attempt login before their corporate HR roster has imported their phone number, resulting in generic 'OTP failed' instead of clear explanation.

Proposed Change:
Graceful session refresh with silent token renewal. Add multi-channel OTP resend (SMS, WhatsApp, Email). If user number is not in enterprise roster, display explicit guidance: 'Your mobile number is not yet registered by your company HR transport team'.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–3: Inspect auth service token TTL and 401 interception logic. Days 4–8: Implement WhatsApp/Email OTP fallback and explicit unrostered error messaging. Days 9–14: QA test and deploy to production auth service.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Multi-channel OTP fallback button appears within 30s.
2. Clear error banner for unrostered numbers explaining HR dependency.
3. Session token auto-renews without logging user out during active shifts.
Metrics to Measure: First-attempt login success rate (proposed target; baseline unknown); drop in OTP-related 1-star reviews.

Summary: One-tap boarding OTP; stop repeated rating prompts after every ride (verify in-app vs Play prompt)
Description:
Affected Flow: Cab Boarding Verification and Post-Trip Completion

Hypotheses:
Extra safety modal popup (seat belt acknowledgement) was placed before OTP display, adding friction during boarding under rain or hurry.
Trip rating modal blocks subsequent app usage with no 'Skip' option, causing commuters to retaliate on the Play Store. (Note: ambiguous whether in-app trip rating or Play Store prompt; verify in app implementation).

Proposed Change:
Display boarding OTP immediately in 1 tap on the main card; make seat belt confirmation non-blocking or inline. Add a clear 'Skip' button to in-app ride ratings; never block app booking or navigation for feedback.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–3: Remove blocking modal on OTP view. Days 4–7: Add dismiss button to post-trip rating. Days 8–14: Release in v12.20.0.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Boarding OTP is visible within 1 tap from active trip card.
2. In-app trip rating dialog has a dismissible 'Skip' button and never blocks app navigation.
3. Verify whether complaints reference in-app trip rating or Play prompt.
Metrics to Measure: Reduction in prompt-frustration 1-star reviews; boarding OTP view latency.

Summary: Reply to 1-2 star reviews within 24h, human-approved, never automatic
Description:
Affected Flow: Google Play Console Developer Response Workflow

Hypotheses:
Lack of Play Console integration into customer support ticketing system leads to 0.71% reply rate (only 3 of 422 low-star reviews received developer responses).
Unacknowledged commuters assume company does not care about reported commute failures.

Proposed Change:
Connect Play Console API to support ticketing (Zendesk/Freshdesk). Institute a human-in-the-loop 24-hour response SLA on all 1–2★ reviews. Replies must be human-approved with specific ticket IDs, never canned automated bots.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–4: Integrate Play Console review webhooks into support queue. Days 5–8: Define human response templates and escalation playbooks. Days 9–14: Train team and launch 24h SLA.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Low-star developer reply rate raised from 0.7% to > 90% (proposed target; baseline unknown).
2. Median response latency < 24 hours.
3. No automated bot replies posted.
Metrics to Measure: Developer reply rate on 1–2★ reviews; updated review star lift.

Description:
Affected Flow: Real-time Vehicle Tracking and Live Map View

Hypotheses:
Driver app background location throttle causes jumpy cab icons and sudden arrivals.
ETA calculation lacks real-time traffic delay push alerts when cab is delayed.

Proposed Change:
Upgrade driver app location foreground service; add client dead-reckoning; push delay alerts if ETA slips by > 5 minutes.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–5: Measure driver GPS dropouts. Days 6–10: Add push delay notification service. Days 11–14: Beta test on selected fleet routes.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Vehicle location update interval <= 10s during active trips.
2. Proactive push notification sent within 60s if vehicle is delayed >= 5m.
3. Smooth map interpolation instead of teleports.
Metrics to Measure: ETA Mean Absolute Error; reduction in tracking-related 1-star reviews.

Summary: Booking failure/wrong date: clearer error reasons
Description:
Affected Flow: Shift Commute Roster Selection and Booking Confirmation

Hypotheses:
Enterprise corporate cutoff policy (e.g. 4-hour advance booking limit) triggers generic failure toasts rather than actionable explanations.
Shift date boundaries cause timezone mismatch during midnight shift scheduling.

Proposed Change:
Display company transport cutoff rules clearly on schedule card. Replace generic failures with exact explanations ('Booking closed at 17:00 as per company policy').

First 14 Days:
Days 1–4: Audit top booking failure codes. Days 5–9: Deploy user-facing error message mapping. Days 10–14: Ship updated booking modal.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. 100% of booking error messages state explicit policy or technical reason.
2. Inline indicator shows cutoff deadline for upcoming shifts.
3. Client-side retry queue on flaky mobile connections.
Metrics to Measure: Booking success conversion rate (proposed target; baseline unknown); booking complaints in reviews.

Summary: One-tap 'what went wrong?' reason picker at trip end
Description:
Affected Flow: Trip Completion and Post-Commute Feedback

Hypotheses:
Users venting with single-word 1-star reviews provide zero diagnostic signal for engineering to act on.
Commuters lack a frictionless 1-tap categorization mechanism inside the app when things go wrong.

Proposed Change:
Introduce a 1-tap post-trip diagnostic picker ('Cab Late', 'App Glitch', 'Driver Issue', 'Routing') at trip completion. Keep Play Store option visible; never suppress or incentivize ratings.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–4: Design 1-tap reason chips. Days 5–9: Implement client feedback screen. Days 10–14: Roll out to pilot accounts.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Reason chips visible upon selecting 1–3 stars on trip end.
2. One tap captures issue category without requiring text typing.
3. No gating or blocking of Play Store rating.
Metrics to Measure: Share of low-star reviews with actionable reasons (aiming to reduce no-reason reviews from 26.1%).

Summary: Route planning, late pickup and driver behaviour: pass evidence to transport operations (not an app fix)
Description:
Affected Flow: Fleet Routing, Vendor Driver Onboarding, and Shift Dispatch SLA

Hypotheses:
Inefficient multi-stop employee clustering generates excessive ride times (60+ minutes for 15km commutes).
Vendor cab drivers mark early no-shows without attempting phone calls to avoid waiting times.

Proposed Change:
Export weekly review evidence dossiers to vendor fleet operations teams; enforce vendor SLA penalties for unattempted no-shows; audit dispatch route clustering algorithms.

First 14 Days:
Days 1–5: Compile fleet vendor feedback report. Days 6–10: Enforce call verification on driver app no-show. Days 11–14: Review route optimization clustering parameters.
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Weekly review feedback dossier automatically delivered to vendor fleet operations leads.
2. Mandatory driver phone attempt logged before driver app allows 'No-Show' trigger.
3. Route circuity index capped at 1.4x direct distance.
Metrics to Measure: Driver-related complaints in reviews; route circuity ratio; vendor SLA breach rates.
